### Problem: Regular expression matching {#sec-st-p4-regex}

::: {.p-statement}
`.` matches any one character. `x*` matches zero or more copies of `x`, where `x` is a letter or `.`. The match is of the whole text. `*` is never alone: it always follows a character.

The official limits keep both strings short (a few tens of characters), and the same table handles thousands. `aa` against `a` is false. `aa` against `a*` is true. `ab` against `.*` is true.

Source: [LC 10 · Regular Expression Matching](https://leetcode.com/problems/regular-expression-matching/){.solved difficulty="Hard"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
`a*` is one token. Treating `a` and `*` as two pattern characters makes `a*` refuse the empty text, because the `a` seems to need a letter. Zero copies of `a*` jumps over both characters. One more copy, when the text letter fits, stays on the same token and consumes one text character.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
- **State.** $dp[i][j]$ = `p[0..j)` matches `s[0..i)`.
- **Transition.** If `p[j - 1]` is `*`, take $dp[i][j - 2]$ (zero copies). If `s[i - 1]` fits `p[j - 2]`, also take $dp[i - 1][j]$.
- **Otherwise** a letter or `.` takes the diagonal when it fits.
- **Base.** $dp[0][0]$ is true. A pattern like `a*b*` can match the empty text by a chain of zero-copy jumps. **Answer.** $dp[n][m]$.
:::

The buttons are in order. Each one keeps the previous solution and changes only what that form changes.

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Recursion

::: {.form-next}
On a `*`, try zero copies first (skip the token) and then one more copy if the current text letter fits. A bare letter or `.` consumes one text character. This is correct, and the `*` branches repeat the same suffixes.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("regex", "rec")
    assert str(final) == "true"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-regex-rec
def regex_rec(s, p):
    def fits(i, j):
        return i < len(s) and (p[j] == "." or p[j] == s[i])

    def f(i, j):
        if j == len(p):
            return i == len(s)
        star = j + 1 < len(p) and p[j + 1] == "*"
        if star:
            if f(i, j + 2):
                return True
            return fits(i, j) and f(i + 1, j)
        return fits(i, j) and f(i + 1, j + 1)

    return f(0, 0)
```

##### C++

```cpp
bool regexFits(int i, int j, const string& s, const string& p) {
    return i < (int)s.size() && (p[j] == '.' || p[j] == s[i]);
}
bool regexRec(int i, int j, const string& s, const string& p) {
    if (j == (int)p.size()) return i == (int)s.size();
    bool star = j + 1 < (int)p.size() && p[j + 1] == '*';
    if (star) return regexRec(i, j + 2, s, p) || (regexFits(i, j, s, p) && regexRec(i + 1, j, s, p));
    return regexFits(i, j, s, p) && regexRec(i + 1, j + 1, s, p);
}
```
:::

#### Memo

::: {.form-next}
Cache the suffix pair. Within the official limits the bare recursion usually finishes, but a pattern with many stars makes it exponential; the memoised form is the one that still makes sense when the strings grow.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("regex", "memo")
    assert str(final) == "true"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-regex-memo
def regex_memo(s, p):
    memo = {}

    def fits(i, j):
        return i < len(s) and (p[j] == "." or p[j] == s[i])

    def f(i, j):
        if (i, j) not in memo:
            if j == len(p):
                memo[i, j] = i == len(s)
            elif j + 1 < len(p) and p[j + 1] == "*":
                memo[i, j] = f(i, j + 2) or (fits(i, j) and f(i + 1, j))
            else:
                memo[i, j] = fits(i, j) and f(i + 1, j + 1)
        return memo[i, j]

    return f(0, 0)
```

##### C++

```cpp
bool regexFits(int i, int j, const string& s, const string& p) {
    return i < (int)s.size() && (p[j] == '.' || p[j] == s[i]);
}
int regexMemo(int i, int j, const string& s, const string& p, vector<vector<int>>& memo) {
    if (memo[i][j] >= 0) return memo[i][j];
    if (j == (int)p.size()) return memo[i][j] = i == (int)s.size();
    if (j + 1 < (int)p.size() && p[j + 1] == '*') {
        bool ok = regexMemo(i, j + 2, s, p, memo);
        if (!ok && regexFits(i, j, s, p)) ok = regexMemo(i + 1, j, s, p, memo);
        return memo[i][j] = ok;
    }
    return memo[i][j] = regexFits(i, j, s, p) && regexMemo(i + 1, j + 1, s, p, memo);
}
```
:::

#### Table

::: {.form-next}
Scan pattern indices. When the current pattern character is `*`, the token is `p[j - 2]` together with the star. Zero copies reads two columns left. One more copy reads the cell above, and only when the text letter fits the token. Row 0 becomes true along `a*b*c*` by those zero-copy jumps.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("regex", "tab")
    assert str(final) == "true"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-regex-tab
def regex_tab(s, p):
    n, m = len(s), len(p)
    dp = [[False] * (m + 1) for _ in range(n + 1)]
    dp[0][0] = True
    for i in range(n + 1):
        for j in range(1, m + 1):
            if p[j - 1] == "*":
                dp[i][j] = dp[i][j - 2]
                if i and (p[j - 2] == "." or p[j - 2] == s[i - 1]):
                    dp[i][j] = dp[i][j] or dp[i - 1][j]
            elif i and (p[j - 1] == "." or p[j - 1] == s[i - 1]):
                dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1]
    return dp[n][m]
```

##### C++

```cpp
bool regexTab(const string& s, const string& p) {
    int n = s.size(), m = p.size();
    vector<vector<char>> dp(n + 1, vector<char>(m + 1));
    dp[0][0] = 1;
    for (int i = 0; i <= n; ++i)
        for (int j = 1; j <= m; ++j) {
            if (p[j - 1] == '*') {
                dp[i][j] = dp[i][j - 2];
                if (i && (p[j - 2] == '.' || p[j - 2] == s[i - 1])) dp[i][j] = dp[i][j] || dp[i - 1][j];
            } else if (i && (p[j - 1] == '.' || p[j - 1] == s[i - 1])) dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1];
        }
    return dp[n][m];
}
```
:::

#### The star token

::: {.form-next}
The table already treats `x*` as one token. This button is that rule checked on the three official samples and on `a*b*c*` against the empty text, which is true, and on `aab` against `a*b*ab`, which the wildcard greedy gets wrong and this token gets right: `a*` takes one `a`, `b*` takes nothing, and `ab` takes the rest.
:::

```{python}

V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}
##### Python

```{python}
#| label: st-regex-star
def regex_star(s, p):
    return regex_tab(s, p)

assert regex_rec("aa", "a*") is True
assert regex_memo("aa", "a") is False
assert regex_tab("ab", ".*") is True
assert regex_star("", "a*b*c*") is True
assert regex_tab("aab", "a*b*ab") is True
assert regex_tab("mississippi", "mis*is*p*.") is False
```

##### C++

```cpp
bool isMatch(const string& s, const string& p) {
    int n = s.size(), m = p.size();
    vector<vector<char>> dp(n + 1, vector<char>(m + 1));
    dp[0][0] = 1;
    for (int i = 0; i <= n; ++i)
        for (int j = 1; j <= m; ++j) {
            if (p[j - 1] == '*') {                     // x* is one token: zero copies, or one more
                dp[i][j] = dp[i][j - 2];
                if (i && (p[j - 2] == '.' || p[j - 2] == s[i - 1])) dp[i][j] = dp[i][j] || dp[i - 1][j];
            } else if (i && (p[j - 1] == '.' || p[j - 1] == s[i - 1])) dp[i][j] = dp[i - 1][j - 1];
        }
    return dp[n][m];
}
```
:::

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Recursion** is usually fast enough inside the official limits and is not the algorithm to keep. **Memoisation** and the **table** are $O(nm)$. The pattern index moves by 1 or by 2, which does not change the bound. Do not run the wildcard greedy here.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- `a*` matches the empty text and also `aaa`.
- `.*` matches every string, including empty.
- A pattern that ends in a letter still has to consume the last text character. Extra text after a match is a failure.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistakes"}
- Splitting `x*` into a letter and a wildcard star. The letter then refuses to match zero times.
- The wildcard greedy. It answers false on `aab` / `a*b*ab`.
- Forgetting row 0. `a*` against the empty string stays false if the zero-copy jump is never applied at `i = 0`.
:::

**Variants.** `x+` is "one or more": write it as `xx*`, so `a+b` becomes `aa*b`. A search that may start and end anywhere, rather than matching the whole text, frees the first column and ORs the last column.

- [LC 44 · Wildcard Matching](https://leetcode.com/problems/wildcard-matching/){difficulty="Hard"}
:::
